claims.claim: Lab tests are reimbursed per billing code under Medicare's Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule, which sets a single national rate per test code with no geographic adjustment.
claims.episode_span: payers reimburse line items that match established CPT codes, so labs price to the code rather than to the marginal cost of the next test

claims.claim: Providers bill far above the Medicare lab rate for the same panel: the average provider charge for a CMP is about $59.85 against a Medicare CLFS payment of $10.33 (a 5.8x markup), supporting the digest's point that hospital-bill figures are inflated list prices.
claims.episode_span: the one-hundred-to-several-hundred-dollar figures that appear on hospital bills are list prices that inflate the ratio another tenfold

claims.claim: Medicare's Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule pays for most clinical diagnostic laboratory tests at the weighted median of private-payor rates, updated about every three years under the Protecting Access to Medicare Act (PAMA).
claims.episode_span: Reimbursement rules further entrench the structure: payers reimburse line items that match established CPT codes
claims.supporting_quote: We pay for most clinical diagnostic laboratory tests (CDLTs) based off the weighted median of private payor rates (fee schedule). Typically, we update the payment rates using private payor rates every 3 years. This is based on The Protecting Access to Medicare Act (PAMA).

claims.claim: CPT codes are the AMA's five-digit code set used across the United States to report procedures and tests to public and private payers, which is why labs price to the code.
claims.episode_span: payers reimburse line items that match established CPT codes, so labs price to the code rather than to the marginal cost of the next test
claims.source_title: CPT billing codes overview | American Medical Association

claims.claim: Under CLIA, a test categorized as waived may be performed by laboratories holding only a Certificate of Waiver; the statute defines waived tests as simple procedures with an insignificant risk of an erroneous result.
claims.episode_span: That move requires demonstrating equivalent accuracy and precision under CLIA-waived or near-waived conditions so that the test can be performed closer to the patient and without the full central-lab overhead.
claims.supporting_quote: When a test is categorized as waived, it allows that test to be performed by laboratories with a Certificate of Waiver (CoW) or a Certificate for Provider Performed Microscopy (PPM) in addition to the other CLIA Certificate types.

claims.claim: Under CLIA every laboratory test system is graded for complexity by scoring seven criteria, with CMS running the CLIA program; the resulting categories are waived, moderate, provider-performed microscopy and high complexity.
claims.episode_span: the analyzer itself must be purchased, validated, and maintained under CLIA or equivalent rules
claims.supporting_quote: Per CLIA, each specific laboratory system, assay , examination is graded for level of complexity by assigning scores of 1, 2, or 3 for each of the following seven criteria. A score of 1 is the lowest level of complexity, and a score of 3 is the highest.
